songs.name: He Was A Friend Of Mine

ai_show_review.summary: Haunting 'Friend' and fiery Viola Lee > The Seven dominate
ai_show_review.blurb: The early show bursts with high‑energy blues and folk, highlighted by a haunting rendition of “He Was A Friend Of Mine” and a scorching “Viola Lee Blues” segue into “The Seven.” Jerry’s guitar swings between brilliant phrasing and raw psychedelic intensity while Phil anchors the groove. The audience tape captures the full set with good clarity despite minor channel wobble.
ai_show_review.review: Port Chester’s Capitol Theater on March 21, 1970 delivered a compact yet potent early‑show that still feels fresh in these audience recordings. From the opening “Walkin' The Dog” through Pigpen‑filled numbers like “Good Lovin’,” the band kept the momentum rolling into an acoustic vibe before launching into one of the night’s high points: a haunting, almost mournful take on “He Was A Friend Of Mine.” Jerry Garcia’s tone on that number was described as both brilliant and eerie, while his lead on the blistering “Viola Lee Blues” – which rolls straight into a seamless “The Seven” with a surprise Cumberland blues segue – showcases his primal psychedelic edge. Phil Lesh provides solid, supportive bass throughout, especially during the spontaneous transitions. The tape, though an audience source with some right‑channel wobble and a brief tape‑curl at the start of Viola Lee > The Seven, remains surprisingly clear and captures the crowd’s enthusiasm, making it the preferred listening version for this historic early‑70s set.

best_recording.reason: Most complete capture of the full early set with good overall clarity despite minor channel wobble; flagged as best by the collection.

band_performance.Jerry: Shows brilliant, haunting phrasing on “He Was A Friend Of Mine” and raw, primal intensity on the “Viola Lee Blues,” though his playing can feel uneven at moments.
